title: Interactive-screen artwork (screens/*.json)
description: Static artwork of an interactive screen, in the package so a mod can replace it. The `id` selects the shape: `boss-arena` is the 256-cell ROUND 10-10 grid; `retry` is the TRY AGAIN / NEW GAME tile, palette and cursor. `map` is the WORLD map's sprite artwork and the castle overlay (its CIRAM cells and sprite groups). `hearth` is the illustration of the two menus ("Where to begin from?" and "What next?"): the sprite groups, the fire and the background bank swap. `castles` is the round-10 castle cinematic of worlds 1..9: per world the clip length, the first clip tick START can skip from and the script's sound requests on clip ticks. `magicword` is "Today's magicword", the `quit` of "What next?": the mode's palette, CHR banks and mask, the VRAM queue capacity, the VRAM record programs of the screen and of the "Will you continue the game?" question (records of count|flags, video address, bytes), the magicword's address, grouping and glyphs, the cursor sprite, the colour cycles and the good-night cinematic's cues, palette and loop. `layouts` is the static picture of the title, the "Where to begin from?" menu, its close and the WORLD map; their dynamic parts are logic. `password` is the magicword screen's message records ("Enter your magicword." and "Error! try again.").

layouts.description: the menu panel's layouts: lists of VRAM records [count|flags, video address, bytes] for "Where to begin from?" and "What next?"

screen.description: the menu screen shown under its panel ("What next?"): the illustration (16 blocks of 4x4 tiles), its attribute block and the palettes (background and sprites); `ppu` are the screen's PPU state words (tile banks, mask, the y=128 split)

duration.description: clip frames: the cinematic window plus the one frame before the level starts

skip_from.description: first clip tick from which START skips

cues.description: [clip tick, request id]: the script's direct sound writes and queue requests, in order

frame_tick_lost.description: clip ticks whose frame the script's setup loses (the counter does not advance)

oneOf.description: `world-clears` is the end-of-world cinematic played when a round-10 clear completes world 1..9 for the first time, and the castle opening that follows world 9's: per clip the length, the first clip tick START can skip from (absent when the script never reads START), the clip ticks whose frame is lost and the script's sound requests. Clips 11..20 are the castle appearance of worlds 1..10: the first clear that fills a world's rounds 1..8 with round 9 or 10 done and its castle flag clear sets that flag and plays the cinematic; the map opens after its last frame.

duration.description: clip frames: the cinematic window plus the one frame after it

skip_from.description: first clip tick from which START skips (absent: not skippable)

cues.description: [clip tick, request id]: the script's direct sound writes and queue requests, in order

frame_tick_lost.description: clip ticks whose frame is lost (the counter does not advance)

oneOf.description: `magicword` is "Today's magicword", the `quit` of "What next?": the mode's palette, CHR banks and mask, the VRAM queue capacity, the VRAM record programs of the screen and of the "Will you continue the game?" question (records of count|flags, video address, bytes), the magicword's address, grouping and glyphs, the cursor sprite, the colour cycles and the good-night cinematic's cues, palette and loop.

Boss's arena background (screens/boss-background.json, loaded by od_arena_load): the two nametables (CIRAM), the room and base palettes, the CHR banks, the 16x16 arena grid, the brightness table and the attack tiles.

`layouts`: the static pictures of the title, the "Where to begin from?" menu, its close and the WORLD map. What changes on these screens is logic in screens.c: the title's input loop and its colour cycle (palette `colour.entry`, indexed by a counter), the menu's fade-in, text and hearth, the close's hearth and fade-out.
